      "title": "Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string \"refresh_token\"",
      "body": "When a token response omits refresh_token (the credential-sync endpoint is explicitly described as returning only access token and expiry), this line writes the literal string \"refresh_token\" into the parsed data. Callers then persist that data (e.g. Office365CalendarService and ZoomVideoApiAdapter) and later use it as the OAuth refresh token, so subsequent refreshes fail with an invalid grant. The existing stored refresh token should be preserved, or the field should be required, not fabricated."
    },

      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "minimumTokenResponseSchema does not validate an expiry field",
      "body": "The computed key `[z.string().toString()]` does not create a dynamic schema for arbitrary numeric fields; it evaluates to a single literal property name (for example `[object Object]`). Since Zod object schemas ignore unknown keys by default, the only real requirement is `access_token`. A credential-sync response with no expiry/expires_in passes validation, and downstream code such as ZoomVideoApiAdapter computes `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)`, storing NaN as the expiry date. The schema must explicitly validate the actual expected expiration field."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Credential-sync mode returns a raw fetch Response, breaking callers",
      "body": "When sync is enabled this returns the native `fetch` `Response`. Original refresh functions return different shapes across callers: Google expects `res?.data`, HubSpot returns a token object and callers read `.expiresIn`, Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM use Axios and callers read `.data`, while Office 365/Webex callers expect a Response and parse it. In sync mode Bigin and ZohoCRM crash at `tokenInfo.data`, HubSpot persists a Response instead of token fields, and Google crashes at `token.access_token`. The helper needs a normalized return contract or each caller must handle the sync-response format explicitly."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Bigin passes credential id instead of user id to credential-sync endpoint",
      "body": "`refreshOAuthTokens` receives `credentialId` as its third argument, but that parameter is `userId` and is sent to the self-hosted sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. The external app store therefore receives the Cal.com database credential id rather than the user id, so it may attach tokens to the wrong user or fail to match an account. The function needs access to `credential.userId` here."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Zoom refresh sends wrong appSlug",
      "body": "The Zoom app id/slug is `zoom` everywhere else in this package (callback uses `appId: \"zoom\"` and redirects to `slug: \"zoom\"`), but credential-sync mode sends `appSlug: \"zoomvideo\"`. A self-hosted app store keyed by the actual Cal.com app slug will not match the Zoom integration."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 106,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Salesforce connection is built with the stale pre-refresh access token",
      "body": "The newly fetched `accessTokenParsed.data` is persisted, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` (the old value) and `credentialKey.instance_url`. If the token was refreshed because it had expired, the first API calls made with this connection still use the expired token. The connection should be built from the refreshed token response fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",

      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Salesforce refresh token flow runs on every CalendarService construction",
      "body": "`getClient` performs an OAuth refresh request and credential update every time a SalesforceCalendarService instance is created, regardless of whether the stored token is still valid. This adds an external API call and database write for each booking operation and may hit Salesforce rate limits. It should refresh only when the token is near or past expiry, or use jsforce's built-in refresh behavior."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Credential find-first then create/update can create duplicates",
      "body": "The endpoint looks up an existing credential with `findFirst` and then either updates or creates it. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both observe no existing row and both insert, leaving duplicate credentials. Since credential selection elsewhere may rely on a single row per user/app, this can cause ambiguity. The operation should be serialized under a transaction/unique constraint or the insert should be idempotent."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 31,
      "severity": "low",

      "title": "Invalid webhook body returns an unhandled 500",
      "body": "`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError for malformed request bodies and there is no try/catch around it. A caller with the correct webhook secret can trigger a 500 and default error page instead of a controlled 400 validation response. Use `safeParse` and return the validation error."
    },
    {
      "file": ".env.example",
      "line": 243,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "Encryption key generation command does not produce a 32-byte key",
      "body": "The comment says CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 32 bytes for AES256, but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`. That command encodes 24 random bytes as a 32-character base64 string; if decoded for use as the AES key it is only 24 bytes, and if used directly as a string the comment is still misleading. Use `openssl rand -base64 32` (which encodes a 32-byte key) instead."
    }

findings.title: Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
findings.body: When a token response omits refresh_token (the credential-sync endpoint is explicitly described as returning only access token and expiry), this line writes the literal string "refresh_token" into the parsed data. Callers then persist that data (e.g. Office365CalendarService and ZoomVideoApiAdapter) and later use it as the OAuth refresh token, so subsequent refreshes fail with an invalid grant. The existing stored refresh token should be preserved, or the field should be required, not fabricated.

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema does not validate an expiry field
findings.body: The computed key `[z.string().toString()]` does not create a dynamic schema for arbitrary numeric fields; it evaluates to a single literal property name (for example `[object Object]`). Since Zod object schemas ignore unknown keys by default, the only real requirement is `access_token`. A credential-sync response with no expiry/expires_in passes validation, and downstream code such as ZoomVideoApiAdapter computes `Math.round(Date.now() + undefined * 1000)`, storing NaN as the expiry date. The schema must explicitly validate the actual expected expiration field.

findings.title: Credential-sync mode returns a raw fetch Response, breaking callers
findings.body: When sync is enabled this returns the native `fetch` `Response`. Original refresh functions return different shapes across callers: Google expects `res?.data`, HubSpot returns a token object and callers read `.expiresIn`, Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM use Axios and callers read `.data`, while Office 365/Webex callers expect a Response and parse it. In sync mode Bigin and ZohoCRM crash at `tokenInfo.data`, HubSpot persists a Response instead of token fields, and Google crashes at `token.access_token`. The helper needs a normalized return contract or each caller must handle the sync-response format explicitly.

findings.title: Bigin passes credential id instead of user id to credential-sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` receives `credentialId` as its third argument, but that parameter is `userId` and is sent to the self-hosted sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. The external app store therefore receives the Cal.com database credential id rather than the user id, so it may attach tokens to the wrong user or fail to match an account. The function needs access to `credential.userId` here.

findings.title: Zoom refresh sends wrong appSlug
findings.body: The Zoom app id/slug is `zoom` everywhere else in this package (callback uses `appId: "zoom"` and redirects to `slug: "zoom"`), but credential-sync mode sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`. A self-hosted app store keyed by the actual Cal.com app slug will not match the Zoom integration.

findings.title: Salesforce connection is built with the stale pre-refresh access token
findings.body: The newly fetched `accessTokenParsed.data` is persisted, but the returned `jsforce.Connection` is constructed with `credentialKey.access_token` (the old value) and `credentialKey.instance_url`. If the token was refreshed because it had expired, the first API calls made with this connection still use the expired token. The connection should be built from the refreshed token response fields.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh token flow runs on every CalendarService construction
findings.body: `getClient` performs an OAuth refresh request and credential update every time a SalesforceCalendarService instance is created, regardless of whether the stored token is still valid. This adds an external API call and database write for each booking operation and may hit Salesforce rate limits. It should refresh only when the token is near or past expiry, or use jsforce's built-in refresh behavior.

findings.title: Credential find-first then create/update can create duplicates
findings.body: The endpoint looks up an existing credential with `findFirst` and then either updates or creates it. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both observe no existing row and both insert, leaving duplicate credentials. Since credential selection elsewhere may rely on a single row per user/app, this can cause ambiguity. The operation should be serialized under a transaction/unique constraint or the insert should be idempotent.

findings.title: Invalid webhook body returns an unhandled 500
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError for malformed request bodies and there is no try/catch around it. A caller with the correct webhook secret can trigger a 500 and default error page instead of a controlled 400 validation response. Use `safeParse` and return the validation error.

findings.title: Encryption key generation command does not produce a 32-byte key
findings.body: The comment says CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY must be 32 bytes for AES256, but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`. That command encodes 24 random bytes as a 32-character base64 string; if decoded for use as the AES key it is only 24 bytes, and if used directly as a string the comment is still misleading. Use `openssl rand -base64 32` (which encodes a 32-byte key) instead.
